aggregation: group rule (all or k of n)

ERQA.Accuracy (multiple-choice): accuracy = correct multiple-choice answers / all questions, in % ('Benchmarks are evaluated by accuracies of multiple-choice answers'); ground truth = manually labeled answers. Answer extraction/matching rule: not stated. Number of runs or sampling settings: not stated. CoT variant appends 'Reason step by step about the answer, and show your work, for each step. Only after that, proceed to the final answer.' No per-category or single- vs multi-image breakdown is reported.

Omni3D-Bench.Accuracy (%) per answer type: Per answer type: % of queries answered correctly, mean over 3 runs (App. B). The correctness rule for count, yes/no and multiple-choice answers (exact string/number match, answer parsing) is not stated. Ground truth: answers computed manually from Omni3D 3D annotations.
Omni3D-Bench.Total accuracy (%): Reported as 'total accuracy', mean over 3 runs. How the per-type scores (including MRA for numeric (other)) are combined is not stated; it is not the unweighted mean of the four type columns (GPT4o: mean(28.1, 35.5, 66.7, 57.2) = 46.9 vs Total 42.9), so presumably a per-query mean, but per-type question counts are not given.
Omni3D-Bench.Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA): MRA = (1/|C|) * sum over theta in C of 1[ |y_hat - y| / y < 1 - theta ], C = {0.5, 0.55, ..., 0.95} (10 thresholds); y_hat = model output, y = ground truth (following VSI-Bench [44]). Averaging over numeric (other) queries is implied but not stated; mean over 3 runs. Parsing of numeric outputs: not stated.
Omni3D-Bench.Oracle accuracy (%): For program-synthesis methods, program correctness is manually verified and used as ground truth on the 50-query subset (true 3D info is not available for all objects); on CLEVR an Oracle Execution Agent uses scene annotations. Per-type correctness rule (including whether numeric (other) uses MRA here) and how Total is combined: not stated.
Omni3D-Bench.Standard deviation across experimental r: Standard deviation of the score across 3 runs, one value per method per benchmark (Table 5; presumably of Total accuracy, not stated). Sample vs population std: not stated.

OmniSpatial.Accuracy (Avg.): accuracy = correct MC answers / questions. Answer checking: non-reasoning models use Manual CoT + regex extraction of a final line 'Answer: X', X in {A,B,C,D}; reasoning models use Manual CoT + GPT-4.1-mini judge (given Question, Pred, GT; replies True/False on the final answer only). Table 7 also compares direct, regex, JSON and LLM-judge extraction. Every model is run 5 times and averaged. Track score = arithmetic mean of its fine-grained sub-task accuracies (Table 11 caption). How Avg. is aggregated is not stated (GPT-4o-mini: Avg 42.64 vs mean of 4 tracks 42.72 vs mean of 10 sub-tasks 43.36, so likely per-question). Fig. 12 bins accuracy by Metric3D-v2 depth and SoFar orientation (single model).
OmniSpatial.Standard deviation over 5 runs: Reported as mean +/- std over the 5 runs per model; sample vs population std: not stated.
OmniSpatial.Rank: Not stated. Values in the extracted Table 2 do not follow Avg. order within a group (e.g., proprietary: Gemini-2.0-flash-exp 48.40 is Rank 2 while GPT-4.1-mini 48.87 is Rank 4), so the ranking rule is unclear; C.2 says the model with the highest average score on the full 8.4K set is Rank 1.
OmniSpatial.Improve: Improve = Avg.(variant) - Avg.(baseline), in accuracy points; baselines: w/o CoT (Table 3), zero-shot CoT (Table 4), zero-shot (Table 5), Manual CoT (Table 12). E.g., Table 5: 48.12 - 40.30 = +7.82; Table 12: 37.19 - 35.59 = +1.60.
OmniSpatial.Inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff': Krippendorff's alpha for multi-annotator agreement; in the human study each item is labeled by 3 of 6 annotators (final answer by majority vote). The alpha formula and implementation are not stated.

SPBench (SpatialLadder).Accuracy (Avg.): Called 'accuracy' (%), but the per-item evaluation rule is NOT stated: the only written rules are for the Stage-3 training reward (MCQ exact match I(o = y), Eq. 3; numerical MRA-style mean over thresholds T = [0.50, ..., 0.95], Eq. 6). The reported numbers suggest MCQ is exact match (values are multiples of 1/n, e.g., MV Rel. Dir. n = 44) and NQ is graded (values not multiples of 1/n, e.g., MV Abs. Dist. n = 30, GPT-4o 12.0). Aggregation is not stated; the tables match Avg. = unweighted mean of task categories (MV GPT-4o: mean(66.3, 12.0, 43.8, 82.4, 36.4) = 48.2) and NQ/MCQ = unweighted mean of their task columns. Answer extraction, decoding and number of runs: not stated. SpatialLadder MV Avg. is 70.9 in Table 1 but 71.2 in Table 10.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Overall (in-domain): Not stated; the numbers match the unweighted mean of the three benchmark Avg. scores (SpatialLadder (45.7 + 70.2 + 70.9)/3 = 62.3; GPT-4o (34.0 + 42.4 + 48.2)/3 = 41.5).
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Improvement / Performance Difference: Improvement = score(SpatialLadder-3B) - score(Qwen2.5-VL-3B), in absolute points (SI Avg.: 70.2 - 40.3 = +29.9), although C.3 calls these 'relative improvements'. Performance Difference = score(ablated variant) - score(full model) per benchmark and Overall.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Format reward r_format: r_format(o) = 1 if o matches the format, else 0. The matching procedure (e.g., regex) is not stated.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Accuracy reward for multiple-choice ques: r_mc(o, y) = I(o = y): strict exact match between predicted option o and ground-truth label y; used when q is in MCQ. Extraction of o from the <answer> tag: not stated.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Accuracy reward for numerical questions: r_num(o, y) = (1/|T|) * sum over tau in T of I( |o - y| / y < tau ), T = [0.50, 0.55, ..., 0.95] (10 thresholds); used when q is in NQ. As written the threshold is tau (credit for relative error below 50%...95%), whereas standard MRA uses 1 - tau (5%...50%); Fig. 3 writes the same '< tau'. Whether this is a typo is not stated. Called a 'weighted relative accuracy measure based on confidence intervals', but no weights appear.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Total reward R(o, y): R(o, y) = r_format(o) + r_accuracy(o, y), with r_accuracy = r_mc if q in MCQ, r_num if q in NQ (range 0 to 2). GRPO advantage A_i = (r_i - mean(r_1..r_G)) / std(r_1..r_G) over G = 8 sampled responses, KL weight beta = 0.01. Cold-start rejection sampling keeps responses with R(o_i, y_i) > 1 + lambda; the value of lambda is not stated.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Reward standard deviation (Reward Std): Standard deviation of the reward per training step; whether it is taken within the GRPO group, over the batch, or over a window is not stated.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Semantic entropy: For each question q, sample 8 responses at temperature 0.9, cluster them by distinct accuracy-reward value (C_k = {o_i : R(o_i) = r_k}), p_i = |C_i| / N, SE(q) = - sum_{i=1..K} p_i log p_i. N is not defined (presumably 8); the question set, the averaging over questions and the log base are not stated.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Visual Attention IoU: IoU_att = sum over visual tokens i in B_obj of a_hat_i / sum over all N visual tokens j of a_hat_j, where B_obj = visual tokens inside the target object's bounding box and a_hat = min-max normalized attention weights (an attention-mass ratio, not a box IoU). Layer/head choice, bounding-box source and averaging over the 400 samples: not stated.
SPBench (SpatialLadder).Visual Attention Entropy: H_att = - sum_{i=1..N} p_i log p_i, where p_i is the probability distribution from normalized attention weights. Normalization, layer/head choice, log base and averaging over samples: not stated.

SpatialBench.Accuracy (ACC): ACC = proportion of predictions that exactly match the ground-truth labels (following VSI-Bench [67]). Answer extraction: not stated. How task scores are combined into a level score M_i ('average rating on each level') is not stated.
SpatialBench.Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA): MRA = (1/10) * sum over theta in Omega of 1[ |y' - y| / y < 1 - theta ], Omega = {0.5, 0.55, ..., 0.95}; y' = prediction, y = ground truth (size/distance answers measured from LiDAR point clouds). Averaging over items is implied but not stated; numeric parsing: not stated.
SpatialBench.Overall Score (capability-oriented): Score = sum_{i=1..5} C_i * M_i, M_i = average rating on level i; C_i = F_i * S_i, F_i = alpha * D_i + 0.1 * (1 - alpha) * E_i, where S_i = standard deviation of model scores on level i (across the evaluated models), D_i = level's question proportion, E_i >= 0 with sum E_j = 10 chosen by minimizing Var(C_{i+1} - C_i) - k * sum_j C_j^2 subject to C_{i+1} >= C_i (strict monotonicity; degenerate solutions discarded), solved with scipy.optimize.minimize. Chosen (alpha, k) = (0.4, 0.01) giving E = (0, 0, 1.4911, 3.8347, 4.6742). The numeric S_i, D_i and resulting C_i are not reported, and how M_i is computed from task scores is not stated.
Not stated. It is neither the unweighted mean of the five level columns (Gemini-2.5-pro: 73.65 vs 71.86) nor of the 15 task columns (70.89), so likely a per-question mean, but this is not stated.
SpatialBench.Rank: Not defined; Table 2 says models are sorted by their overall Rank, and the ranks match descending Overall Score (Gemini-2.5-pro 75.79 -> 1, ..., Qwen2.5-VL-7B 17.45 -> 15).
SpatialBench.Delta change (few-shot vs default): Delta = score(few-shot/one-shot setting) - score(default), in points (Table 4; bold if Delta > +10). Section 5.3 calls the setting one-shot while Table 4 calls it few-shot.

MindCube.QA Accuracy: QA Accuracy = N_correct / N_total x 100%, over all questions evaluated. Overall is pooled over questions, not a mean of settings (e.g. Raw-QA 37.81 = (0.34x200 + 0.36x600 + 0.452x250)/1050). The model must output one option (e.g. 'A. above', or inside <answer></answer> for reasoning configs); the answer-parsing / matching rule is not stated. Occlusion analysis reports relative accuracy drops (50.7% fully visible -> fully occluded, p<0.01; test not stated).
MindCube.Coverage (Cov): Cov = |O_c| / |O*|, where O* = ground-truth map objects, O_g = generated map objects, O_c = O* intersect O_g; in [0,1]. How objects are matched between maps (name matching) is not stated; averaging over maps not stated.
Relation dir(oi,oj): right if |xj-xi|>|yj-yi| and xj>xi; left if |xj-xi|>|yj-yi| and xj<xi; down if |yj-yi|>=|xj-xi| and yj>yi; up if |yj-yi|>=|xj-xi| and yj<yi; inner if ||pj-pi||2 < delta and (fi=inner or fj=outer); outer if ||pj-pi||2 < delta and (fi=outer or fj=inner); else null; delta = 0.5 (precedence when a close pair also meets a direction case not stated). P* = {(oi,oj) in O_c x O_c, i!=j, R*(oi,oj) != null}; S_dir = |{(oi,oj) in P*: R_g(oi,oj) = R*(oi,oj)}| / |P*|, in [0,1], computed at the best-aligned rotation from R (all 90-degree turns about z, one 90-degree turn about x and about y). Mean over maps; treatment of invalid maps or empty P* not stated.
MindCube.Facing similarity (S_face, Avg. Facing S: F* = {oi in O_c | f*_i != null}; S_face = |{oi in F*: f^g_i = f*_i}| / |F*|, in [0,1]; facing labels in {up, right, down, left, inner, outer}; at the best-aligned rotation. Mean over maps; handling of empty F* or invalid maps not stated.
MindCube.Overall Similarity: S_overall = alpha x S_dir + (1 - alpha) x S_face, alpha = 0.7, in [0,1], using the best-aligned rotation among R; reported as a percentage averaged over generated maps (averaging and invalid-map handling not stated).
MindCube.Isomorphic Rate (rotation-invariant isom: Rotation set R = all 90-degree turns about z plus one 90-degree turn about x and about y. A map is isomorphic if there exists k such that for all oi, oj in O*: R*(oi,oj) = R_g^(k)(oi,oj), where R_g^(k) is the relation matrix after applying R_k. Rate = percentage of maps isomorphic to the ground truth; denominator (all vs valid maps) and treatment of objects missing from the generated map not stated.
MindCube.Valid Rate (graph validity): A map is valid if (1) it is well-formed JSON, (2) all fields conform to expected formats and constraints, and (3) at least one object has a valid position; Valid Rate = percentage of valid maps.
MindCube.CC (Both Correct): Each pair (primary question, paired question with changed central-object attributes or number of central objects, same peripheral scene) is classed CC if both answers are correct; CC = count(CC pairs) / number of pairs. Number of pairs per test not stated.
MindCube.WW (Both Wrong): Pair classed WW if both the primary and the paired question are answered wrongly; WW = count(WW pairs) / number of pairs (CC + WW + IC = 1).
MindCube.IC (Inconsistent) / inconsistency score: Pair classed IC if one version is answered correctly and the other wrongly; IC = count(IC pairs) / number of pairs.
MindCube.RL reward (format +1, correct answer +5): reward = 1 x 1[output structurally valid, e.g. cognitive map follows the predefined schema] + 5 x 1[final answer correct]. Ablation (Table 16): (+0,+5) answer-only and (+5,+0) format-only variants. Exact validity checks and answer matching not stated; 8 trajectories per rollout, max 1 turn.

MMSI-Bench.Accuracy: Exact match between the option letter extracted from the model output (prompted to enclose the letter in a marker) and the ground-truth option; if the output is not in the required format, the LLM-based fallback extractor of VLMEvalKit is used. Temperature 0, max 2,048 output tokens. Avg. appears pooled over questions (not stated; e.g. o3: mean of the 11 category scores = 41.6 but reported Avg. 41.0, which matches the question-weighted mean).
MMSI-Bench.Reasoning accuracy (automated reasoning-: An MLLM judge receives images, question, the model's reasoning, the correct answer and the human-annotated reference reasoning (each step tagged with its reasoning type) and outputs one category: 1 grounding, 2 overlap-matching/scene-reconstruction, 3 situation-transformation, 4 spatial-logic error, 5 completely correct. Reasoning accuracy = share labeled 5 (implied, formula not written). The judge model for the full run is not named (GPT-4o in the validation test); judge decoding settings not stated.
MMSI-Bench.Error-type distribution: Same judge call as reasoning accuracy: one category (1-4 error, 5 correct) per question, most critical error only; share = count(category) / number of questions. Exact per-type numbers only in Figure 7; manual 100-sample analysis gives no numbers in text.
MMSI-Bench.Error-type labeling accuracy of the auto: Fraction of selected samples where GPT-4o's error-type label is correct; the reference labels (presumably the manual categorization) and the number of selected samples are not stated. Prompts in Tables 8 and 9.
MMSI-Bench.Pearson correlation with EmbodiedBench: Pearson coefficient between per-model MMSI-Bench Avg. accuracy and per-model score on each EB task over the 9 models in Table 11; how the EB scores are computed is not stated in this paper.
MMSI-Bench.Spearman correlation with EmbodiedBench: Spearman rank coefficient between per-model MMSI-Bench Avg. accuracy and per-model EB task score over the 9 models in Table 11; tie handling not stated.

SPAR-Bench.Avg. (overall SPAR-Bench score) with Low: Not stated in text; table values equal the unweighted mean of the 20 per-task scores, mixing MRA (9 numeric tasks) and accuracy (11 choice tasks) (e.g. Human 67.27, GPT-4o full 38.11). Level score = mean of its task scores; Rank = order by Avg. The paper notes level scores are not directly comparable because the metrics differ.
SPAR-Bench.Accuracy: Not stated beyond 'classification tasks are evaluated using accuracy' (correct / total per task); answer extraction and matching not stated. Random and frequency chance levels reported per task.
SPAR-Bench.MRA (called 'mean relative absolute erro: Not stated: the paper only names it 'mean relative absolute error (MRA)'. Tables report it on 0-100 with higher = better (e.g. Human 72.75 on Depth-OC), consistent with VSI-Bench-style Mean Relative Accuracy, but the formula, confidence thresholds and handling of unparsable answers are not given (trait values inferred).
SPAR-Bench.Average Position Error (APE) on BEV coor: Object-level error between predicted and ground-truth BEV (x, y) in an observer-centric frame (origin = first-view camera center projected to the ground, y along viewing direction, x to the right); distance function not stated (presumably Euclidean, meters). Mean, median (P50) and 90th percentile (P90) over objects; bins [0,1), [1,2), [2,3), [3,5), [5,7), [7,10), [10,inf) m. 1,000 ScanNet++ val samples, 3 images and 3-7 objects each; handling of missing/unparsable objects not stated.

MMSI-Video-Bench.Exact-match accuracy: Correct = 1[extracted option == ground-truth option] ('a prediction is considered correct only if it exactly matches the ground-truth'); options parsed from the output by a general-purpose answer extraction function; accuracy = mean over questions x 100. How Avg. is aggregated (question-weighted vs mean of subtypes) is not stated. Difficulty levels are assigned per question from 'the overall accuracy of all models on each question'; the easy/medium/hard cut-offs are not stated. Random-guessing baseline about 24%.
MMSI-Video-Bench.Human-AI Gap: Human-level accuracy minus the best model's accuracy, in percentage points: 96.4 (human) - 38.0 (Gemini 3 Pro) = 58.4 ('nearly 60%'). The table caption only says 'the performance difference as a percentage'; which input track the model score comes from is not stated.
MMSI-Video-Bench.Error type distribution: 520 incorrectly answered cases from 4 models (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, O3, QwenVL2.5-72B), evenly sampled across question categories; models are asked to output an answer plus a reason; each case is assigned one of five non-overlapping error types; proportion = cases of a type / all analysed cases (overall) or / cases in that category. Who assigns the error type (human or model) is not stated.

OSI-Bench.Accuracy (ACC): Correct = 1[extracted option == ground-truth option]; the prompt asks for a single letter, with a regex fallback that takes the last valid option in the output; greedy decoding (temperature 0); mean over questions. Four-choice chance baseline = 25.0. How Avg. (and Rank) combine ACC and MRA across the nine tasks is not stated.
OSI-Bench.Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA): MRA = (1/10) * sum over theta in C = {0.05, 0.10, ..., 0.50} of 1[|y_hat - y| / y < theta] (a step-wise score). Near-zero ground truth (dynamic tasks): if y < ST and y_hat < ST the score is 1.0; if y < ST and y_hat >= ST the relative error uses the denominator floored to ST, i.e. |y_hat - y| / ST. The value of ST is not stated ('a small value'). The number is taken as the last numeric value in the output (regex fallback). Baseline for NA tasks is defined as 0 (the frequency chance level is rejected as a ground-truth leak).
OSI-Bench.Performance gain of vision-enabled over: Gain = score(vision enabled) - score(vision disabled), in points, using each task's own metric (ACC for MCA, MRA for NA); Fig. 1 drop = MRA(no vision) - MRA(vision). Human gain measured on a small subset. No threshold for 'reliance on vision' is stated.
OSI-Bench.Abnormal-scene drop (Drop, Normal to Abn: Drop = MRA(Normal Set) - MRA(Abnormal Set), in points; 20 Blender scenes, 120 template questions per set, ground truth from engine metadata. Overall = aggregation not stated (Tab. 6 values equal the mean of Size and Distance, e.g. (37.3 + 54.7)/2 = 46.0). The text (L1175) quotes Gemini size 54.7 to 28.3, while Tab. 6 lists 29.7 for Gemini (28.3 is the Qwen value).
OSI-Bench.Performance gain across model generation: Gain = score(newer version) - score(older version) at a similar parameter scale, 32 input frames (e.g. +24.1 on VSI-Bench for InternVL3.5-38B over InternVL2-40B; Fig. 4c: MRA change on absolute distance). Models are grouped by approximate parameter scale; the exact pairing rule is not stated.

PAI-Bench (understanding).Accuracy: A lightweight LLM (Qwen3-8B) post-processes each full response to extract the final letter option; correct = 1[extracted option == annotated answer]; accuracy = mean over questions x 100. Input: 16 frames (InternVL3.5: 8). How Avg. and Overall are aggregated is not stated (the random-guess row in Tab. 5 is consistent with a question-weighted mean: Common Sense 38.9, Overall 37.0). Random-guess baseline: 37.0 Overall.
PAI-Bench (understanding).Accuracy vs number of input frames (0-fr: Same accuracy as the main metric, recomputed at each frame count; 0 frames = question text only. The benchmark is called unbiased because 0-frame accuracy falls to about random-guess level and 1-frame accuracy is well below 32-frame accuracy; no numeric threshold is stated.
PAI-Bench (understanding).Thinking-mode gain: Gain = accuracy(thinking on) - accuracy(thinking off), in points, shown in parentheses; for GPT-5, thinking on = medium reasoning effort, off = minimal reasoning effort.

VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Accuracy (vision-enabled, 'Vis.'): Not stated: the paper reports one 'accuracy' over the whole benchmark, which mixes multiple-choice and open-ended numerical questions (counting, object size, absolute distance, room size), and never says how numerical answers are scored (MRA is not mentioned) or whether partial credit is given. Chance (frequency) baseline = 34.0.
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Blind accuracy: Same scoring as vision-enabled accuracy (not stated) with the visual input removed; the model receives only question text and answer choices.
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Vision-Blind Gap (Delta V-B): Delta V-B = Accuracy(Vis.) - Accuracy(Blind), in points (e.g. 16.6 on VSI-Bench-Debiased vs 12.4 on the original after fine-tuning); the relative widening is reported as a percent: (16.6 - 12.4) / 12.4 = about 34% wider.
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Increase due to fine-tuning (Delta due t: Delta = score after VSI-Train-10k fine-tuning - score of base LLaVA-Video-7B, in points, separately for Vis., Blind and Delta V-B (e.g. +20.4 vision vs +18.8 blind on the original; +17.4 vs +11.7 on VSI-Bench-Debiased).
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Overall TsT Accuracy (TsT-LLM CV-Acc., T: Split the test set into k = 5 disjoint folds; train on k-1 folds and predict the held-out fold; repeat k times so every sample gets an out-of-fold prediction; TsT accuracy = accuracy aggregated over all folds (also reported as mean +/- std across folds). TsT-LLM: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with LoRA (r = 128, alpha = 256, lr 5e-5 cosine, batch 32, 3 epochs) on question and choice text only. TsT-RF: scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier (1000 trees, max depth 20) on hand-crafted non-visual features computed from training folds only. How an open-ended numerical prediction is counted as correct is not stated. Read as a lower bound on exploitability.
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Delta TsT: Delta TsT = TsT-LLM cross-validated accuracy - zero-shot blind accuracy of the same LLM (Qwen2.5-7B) before fine-tuning, in points (VSI-Bench: 56.4 - 25.0 = +31.4).
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Sample-level bias score s(x): s(x) = the diagnostic model's confidence (predicted probability) for the ground-truth answer when x is in the held-out fold of k = 5 cross-validation (TsT-LLM: predicted probability of the ground-truth answer; VSI-Bench-Debiased used TsT-RF scores). IBP: recompute s(x) on the remaining set, remove a batch of size b chosen by SelectBatch (highest s(x), weighted sampling for numerical tasks, or group-aware balancing), repeat until removal budget B is used or max s(x) <= tau. The values of B, b and tau are not stated (937 of 3,056 questions removed).
VSI-Bench-Debiased (VSI-Bench-U).Gini importance: Gini importance of each feature in the TsT-RF random forest (cited method; formula not stated in the paper).

VSTI-Bench.Accuracy (ACC): Correct if the predicted option matches the ground truth 'via exact or fuzzy matching' (the fuzzy rule is not stated); mean over questions. How Avg. is aggregated is not stated (the human and chance rows of Tab. 2 equal the unweighted mean of the five task scores, e.g. (51.4 + 46.8 + 95.1 + 97.5 + 94.3)/5 = 77.0). Random chance for movement direction = mean over questions of 1/(number of choices); a frequency chance level is also reported.
VSTI-Bench.Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA): MRA = (1/10) * sum over theta in {0.50, 0.55, ..., 0.95} of 1[|y_hat - y| / y < 1 - theta]; ground truth computed from 3D boxes and camera poses (ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes). Handling of near-zero ground truth (e.g. tiny displacement) is not stated.

DSI-Bench.Sample-wise accuracy: Correct = 1[selected option == ground-truth option], read directly from the output without any external model or judge; accuracy = correct / all augmented samples. Random baseline = 25% (4 options). For 3D expert models (VGGT, SpatialTrackerV2) the predicted observer/object trajectories are mapped to answer choices by a rule-based procedure (orientation questions removed). How Overall is aggregated is not stated.
DSI-Bench.Group-wise accuracy: A group = the 4 flip variants of one original video and question; group correct = 1[number of correct variants >= 3 of 4]; group-wise accuracy = correct groups / all groups. The random baseline is printed as '0.05%'; for p = 0.25 per variant, P(>= 3 of 4) = 4 x 0.25^3 x 0.75 + 0.25^4 = about 0.051, so the printed value looks like a fraction with a stray % sign (the paper does not explain it).
DSI-Bench.Static vs dynamic performance gap: Gap = accuracy(static condition) - accuracy(dynamic condition), in points (e.g. Seed-1.6-vision: 2.67 lower for object dynamics with a moving observer, 11.55 lower for observer motion).
DSI-Bench.Free-form reasoning gain (FFR Delta): Delta = overall accuracy(FFR) - overall accuracy(RAWQA), in points (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL-72B +0.2).
DSI-Bench.Forward-option selection proportion (for: Over all VQA pairs whose options contain the string 'forward': model proportion = questions where the model chose a 'forward' option / all such questions, compared with the proportion of ground-truth answers containing 'forward'; bias = model proportion far above the ground-truth proportion; no numeric threshold stated.

BLINK.Accuracy: All tasks are recast as multiple choice. The chosen option is extracted from the model output first by exact matching of the option label (e.g. 'C' or '(C)'), then, if that fails, by GPT-3.5-turbo, which maps the prediction to one of the options or to 'Z' (no match). An item is correct if 1[extracted option = ground-truth option]. Task accuracy = #correct / #questions in the task. The overall score is the average over tasks: Appendix C.4 says 'averaged across all task', but the Table 1 overall formula is not written out. Decoding follows VLMEvalKit with temperature 0 and retry 10. The random-choice row is the expected accuracy of guessing.
BLINK.Self-consistency score: GPT-4V is run 5 times at temperature 1.0 and the answers are combined by self-consistency (Wang et al. [78]). The voting rule and tie-break are not stated; the standard method is a majority vote. The resulting accuracy is averaged across all tasks (48.38%) and compared with the mean single-run accuracy over the 5 runs (38.15%).
BLINK.Error analysis (error-type distribution): 10 error instances per task (140 total) are sampled at random and examined by hand. Share per category = #errors in the category / 140. Appendix C.3 categories: recognition failure on small regions 28.5%, failure to locate the circled point 20%, spatial relations 14.3%, reasoning errors 12.9%, scene impression 8.6%, refusal 6.4%, grounding 5.7%. The main text uses a different grouping: hallucinated fine-grained patterns 24.2%, hallucinated visual-prompt locations 20.0%, overall setting or style 8.6%, grounding 5.7%. The annotation protocol and the number of annotators are not stated.
BLINK.Common mistakes (error overlap between m: The paper reports raw counts of items answered incorrectly by both models of a pair, e.g. LLaVA-v1.5-7B (1187 mistakes) and LLaVA-v1.5-13B (1147 mistakes) share 899, and LLaVA-v1.5-7B shares 959 with LLaVA-internLM2-7B, 782 with Qwen-VL-Max and 655 with GPT-4V. There is no normalisation, and the split (val or test) is not stated.

SpatialTree.Avg. (hierarchical weighted score): Bottom-up weighted sum: score(parent) = sum over children of w_child * score(child), applied recursively up to the root. Level weights: L1 = L2 = L3 = L4 = 0.25. L2: Understanding 0.7, Memory 0.3. L3: Causal Reasoning 0.65, Sequential Planning 0.35. L4: Goal Execution 0.5, Open Exploration 0.5. The L1 weights disagree between sources. Table 1 uses Geometry 0.40, Motion 0.15, Relation 0.15, Localization 0.20, Orientation 0.10. Appendix Fig. H lists Geometry 0.5, Motion 0.1, Relation 0.15, Localization 0.2, Orientation 0.1, which sums to 1.05. The weights come from cognitive-hierarchy priors plus the Pearson-correlation heatmap. How the per-task metrics inside one leaf ability are combined into the leaf score is not stated.
SpatialTree.Multi-option QA accuracy (classification: Accuracy = #(predicted choice = ground-truth option) / #questions. Answer extraction or parsing is not stated.
SpatialTree.Numeric QA relative error / Mean Relativ: Relative Error = |y_hat - y| / |y| (appendix). The main text calls the numeric score 'mean relative accuracy (MRA)' but gives no threshold set and no rule for turning relative error into the 0-100 table score (not stated).
SpatialTree.Mean Squared Error (MSE) for distance es: Named only. No formula is given (presumably the mean of (y_hat - y)^2), and how it is converted to the 0-100 table score is not stated. This conflicts with the appendix, which scores numeric QAs by relative error.
SpatialTree.Gaussian-kernel orientation score (angle: For each parameter: S(y_pred, y_gt, sigma_gt) = exp(-(y_pred - y_gt)^2 / (2 * sigma_gt^2)), where sigma_gt is the uncertainty GeoCalib outputs for its own label. S = 1 for an exact match and decays towards 0. Task score = mean of S over pitch, roll and vFOV. Object orientation is 'similar', over azimuth, polar and rotation; the sigma source for OrientAnything labels is not stated. The main text also refers to this as 'angular difference for orientation tasks'.
SpatialTree.GPT Judge (LLM-as-a-Judge): A GPT-based judge decides whether the response meets the task requirements, 'optionally scoring partial correctness'. The judge model, prompt, score scale and the way the hybrid multi-option + judge scores are combined are not stated.
SpatialTree.Step-wise navigation accuracy s_step: For each step, with predicted and ground-truth translation vectors dp_pred and dp_gt: s_d = max(0, 1 - ||dp_pred - dp_gt|| / ||dp_gt||); s_theta = (dp_pred . dp_gt) / (||dp_pred|| * ||dp_gt||); s_step = s_d * max(0, s_theta), in [0, 1]. The number of steps is capped at 10. Step scores are 'aggregated across all steps'; whether that is a sum or a mean, and how mismatched sequence lengths are handled, is not stated.
SpatialTree.Goal-driven manipulation step score: Translation reuses s_step = s_d * max(0, s_theta) from navigation. Rotation: R_err = R_pred * R_gt^T, theta_err = arccos((Tr(R_err) - 1) / 2), s_rot = max(0, 1 - theta_err / pi). Gripper: s_gripper = 1[predicted open/close state = ground truth]. Per-step score = weighted combination of s_step, s_rot and s_gripper; the weights are not stated, and neither is the aggregation over steps.
SpatialTree.Success rate: Not stated: no success criterion or formula is given. It is presumably #successful episodes / #episodes.
SpatialTree.Cognitive map accuracy: Not stated: only the name is given. Ground-truth maps come from BEV maps made by 3D reconstruction pipelines. The matching rule and whether partial credit is given are not stated.
SpatialTree.Pearson correlation between sub-abilitie: Pearson correlation coefficient between pairs of sub-ability benchmark scores, computed across all evaluated models and shown as a heatmap (Fig. 5).
SpatialTree.Hierarchy-Aware Reward (RLVR / GRPO): Verifiable reward for the correct discrete MCQ selection ('the training objective is purely maximizing the reward on discrete MCQ selection'). For intuitive perception tasks (depth, counting, orientation), the reward for thinking is removed and a length penalty is added. For complex reasoning tasks (navigation planning, causal reasoning), rewards for explicit reasoning steps are kept and amplified. Reward values, the form of the length penalty, the reasoning-reward definition and the weights are not stated.

ViewSpatial-Bench.Accuracy: Accuracy = #(prediction = ground-truth answer) / #questions, zero-shot, with the prompt 'Reply only to the corresponding option'. Each model is evaluated 5 times and the mean over runs is reported. Answer parsing is not stated. The perspective Avg. and Overall values in Table 2 equal the item-count-weighted mean of the task accuracies (i.e. a mean over items); this matches the numbers but is not stated in the text. VSI-Bench follows its original protocol (lmms-eval, 32 frames). How direct-answer outputs are matched is not stated. The random-chance level is 26.33%.
ViewSpatial-Bench.VSI-App accuracy (majority vote over opt: For each question, 5 different option orderings are generated and each model is tested once on each. The final prediction is the option chosen most often across the 5 tests (majority vote; tie-break not stated). Accuracy = #(voted answer = ground truth) / #questions, reported for indoor and outdoor and as their average.

CVBench.Accuracy: An item is correct if the chosen option = the ground-truth option; answer extraction is not stated. The Average column equals the item-count-weighted mean over tasks (i.e. a mean over items); this matches Table 4 but is not stated in the text. Open-source models get 8 frames per video. A random-choice row is reported.
CVBench.Performance change under input perturbat: delta = accuracy(normal input) - accuracy(perturbed input). This is computed for (a) randomly disordered video order and (b) a single randomly selected video, reported for 3 runs and averaged (e.g. 46.8 -> 42.3, average delta 4.5; 46.8 -> 37.5, average delta 9.3). Table 6 gives the delta between 224x224 and 448x448 inputs at 8, 16 and 32 frames, and between frame counts.

PerceptionComp.Accuracy: An item is correct if the final answer matches the ground truth. For models with complex reasoning, the intermediate reasoning and verbose output are cut out programmatically, and Gemini-2.5-Flash acts as judge: it gets the ground-truth answer and the extracted response and decides whether they match (semantic equivalence and factual consistency). Accuracy = #correct / #questions. Overall aggregation is not stated.
PerceptionComp.First-error step distribution (incorrect: Each failed question is split into a fixed sequence of subcondition-solving steps, following the annotated subconditions. The first step where the model's intermediate conclusion diverges from the expert trace is marked. Share per step = #failures whose first error is at that step / #failures analysed. The text gives 5% at Step 1, 20% at Step 2, 40% at Step 3, 25% at Step 4 and 10% after that. Fig. 11a (Gemini-3-Pro) gives 11.1 / 29.6 / 31.5 / 20.4 / 7.4%. Who judges divergence, and how many failures were sampled, is not stated; the 'protocol in supp.' is not found in the paper.
PerceptionComp.Error cause distribution: Failures of Gemini-3-Pro are assigned to causes: spatial understanding 31.5%, static feature perception 29.6%, incomplete reasoning 14.8%, counting errors 13.0%, dynamic feature perception 11.1%. Share = #failures with that cause / #failures analysed; the number analysed is not stated. Separately, expert review attributes 60% of mid-chain failures to violated spatial subconditions.

Video-MME.Accuracy: The option letter is extracted from the model output with regular expressions and compared directly with the ground-truth answer; no external LLM judge (e.g. ChatGPT) is used. Accuracy = #correct / #questions. The overall aggregation across duration subsets is not stated. Subtitle and audio gains are differences in accuracy.

Video-MME-v2.Non-Lin Score (group-level non-linear sc: Overall = (1/|G|) * sum over groups g of S(g). Each group has 4 questions with 8 options each. S(g) = (N/4)^2 for consistency groups, where N is the number correct out of 4. For coherence groups, S(g) uses first-error truncation: only the consecutive correct answers counted from the first step score, and anything after the first error is ignored. The mapping from that run length to S(g) is not stated. Table values are on a 0-100 scale. Level scores are means over the groups in that level (implied, not written out).
Video-MME-v2.Capability consistency score (Consistenc: Mean over consistency groups of (N/4)^2, where N is the number of correct answers out of 4. So 4/4 -> 1, 3/4 -> 0.5625, 2/4 -> 0.25, 1/4 -> 0.0625, 0 -> 0, which suppresses isolated lucky guesses.
Video-MME-v2.Reasoning coherence score (Coherence): First-error truncation: starting from Q1, only the run of consecutive correct answers counts, and any correct answer after the first error earns nothing. Group scores are averaged over coherence groups. How the run length k maps to a score (e.g. k/4 or (k/4)^2) is not stated.
Video-MME-v2.Average Accuracy (Avg Acc): AvgAcc = (1/|Q|) * sum over questions q of 1[y_hat_q = y_q], over 8-option questions (random guess 12.5%). Answer extraction is not stated.
Video-MME-v2.Robustness Ratio (Non-Lin Score / Avg Ac: Ratio = Non-Lin Score / Avg Acc per model (e.g. Gemini-3-Pro 49.4 / 66.1 = about 75%). Gap = Avg Acc - Non-Lin Score.
Video-MME-v2.Q1-Q4 accuracy (per-position accuracy tr: Accuracy over all questions at position q (q = 1..4) in the given group type. The formula is not written out; it is implied by 'Q1-Q4 overall accuracy'.
Video-MME-v2.Mean-variance of Q1-Q4 accuracy (capabil: Mean and variance of the four per-position accuracies Q1-Q4 in consistency groups, per model. The variance formula (population or sample) is not stated.

SpatialRGPT-Bench.Success rate (qualitative QA, GPT-4 judg: GPT-4 receives the question, the correct answer and the model response and outputs a score of 0 or 1 for whether the response aligns with the correct answer; success rate = mean of the 0/1 scores over the items of a category, with 'failed to answer' counted as incorrect (accuracy = correct vs incorrect or failed to answer). An across-category average is not defined in the text. The exact GPT-4 prompt is only in a table (Table 12) whose body is not in the md.
SpatialRGPT-Bench.Success rate (quantitative QA, within +/: GPT-4 extracts the numeric values from the correct answer and from the model response and converts both to the same unit (meters); success = 1[pred within +/-25% of gt], i.e. 1[|pred - gt| <= 0.25 * gt]; success rate = mean over items per category. Not stated: whether items with no numeric answer count as failures in the success rate, whether the boundary is inclusive, and how the rule applies to non-metric answers such as o'clock directions in the QA templates.
SpatialRGPT-Bench.Absolute relative error: GPT-4 converts both values to meters; the formula is not written in the paper (only named, citing [42, 43]); the standard form is |pred - gt| / gt per item, averaged over items. Answers that failed to produce a numerical response are excluded from the calculation.

SpatialEval.Accuracy: Accuracy = (# questions answered correctly) / (# questions), averaged over all questions of a task ('Avg Acc'). For non-deterministic decoding (top-p) the result is averaged over three independent runs for open-source models (error bars from the three runs); proprietary models get one run. A dashed line marks the expected accuracy of random guessing. Not stated: how the chosen option is extracted from the free-text response (the prompt asks for a one-sentence answer followed by a step-by-step explanation).
SpatialEval.Modality gap: Modality gap = Acc(VTQA) - Acc(VQA). Not stated: how it is averaged across models and tasks to give the single 7.0% and 30.0% figures.
SpatialEval.Accuracy difference between paired setti: Difference of task-averaged accuracies between the two settings, in percentage points (e.g. Mistral-7B 62.1% vs LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B 47.1% = 15% drop; LLaVA-1.6-34B +20.1% with no image; LLaVA-1.6-Vicuna-13B +6.5% with a noise image; GPT-4V +25.6% from VQA to VTQA). Spider plots show each pair's Avg Acc per task.

MMPerspective.Accuracy (per task; P Acc, R Acc): Task accuracy = (# correct) / (# questions); each question has one correct answer; answer options are randomly shuffled at dataset creation; greedy decoding for open-source models and deterministic API modes for proprietary models. P Acc and R Acc: aggregation not stated; the Table 1 values equal the unweighted mean of the 4 perception-task and 5 reasoning-task accuracies (e.g. InternVL2.5-2B: (47.4+22.8+13.0+65.3)/4 = 37.1). Answer extraction from the model output is not stated.
MMPerspective.Overall accuracy (P&R Overall): Not stated in the text. The Table 1 values equal the unweighted mean of the 9 task accuracies (e.g. InternVL2.5-2B: 339.1/9 = 37.7). They do not match the item-weighted mean or the mean of P Acc and R Acc.
MMPerspective.Binary P'Robust Score: Binary-Robust = (1/|S|) * sum over seeds (I_s, q, a*) in S of 1[ AND over I in V_s of M(I, q) = a* ], where V_s = {I_s} U {I_1..I_n_s} is the original image plus all its perturbed variants. A seed scores 1 only if every image in its set is answered correctly (e.g. 4 of 5 correct gives 0). Number of variants per seed n_s is not stated.
MMPerspective.Graded P'Robust Score: Graded-Robust = (1/|S|) * sum over seeds in S of ( (1/|V_s|) * sum over I in V_s of 1[M(I, q) = a*] ); e.g. 4 of 5 images correct gives 0.8 for that set.
MMPerspective.Accuracy change from Chain-of-Thought (D: Delta = score with CoT - score without CoT, in percentage points, per model and column; 'Average Delta' = mean of the three models' Deltas (e.g. +5.59 Overall, +6.63 Robustness). The one-shot ICL study (Table 4) reports raw accuracies under the same metrics, not a Delta.
MMPerspective.Correlation of performance with model /: Correlation coefficient r between model (or encoder) parameter count and Overall accuracy or robustness across evaluated models. Not stated: the correlation type (Pearson assumed from 'r'), whether size is log-scaled, and which robustness score (Binary or Graded) is used.
MMPerspective.Error-pattern phi coefficient (with Cohe: Phi coefficient between two models' correctness on the same questions (the phi formula is not written; the standard form is Pearson correlation of the two binary correct/incorrect vectors). Within-family vs cross-family phi distributions are compared with Cohen's d = 0.33, p < 0.001. The significance test used is not stated.
MMPerspective.Question difficulty level: Per question: proportion of models that answered it correctly, then binned into four difficulty levels. The bin thresholds are not stated.

Anywhere3D-Bench.Acc@0.25IoU: Boxes are [center_x, center_y, center_z, size_x, size_y, size_z]. IoU (Eq. 1/B1): if level = area, IoU = 2D IoU on the xy (horizontal) plane; else if the GT size along some axis i in {x,y,z} is < t, IoU = 2D IoU over the other two axes * 1[|center_i^gt - center_i^pred| < t AND size_i^pred < t]; otherwise 3D IoU. t = 0.05 m, k = 0.25; Acc@kIoU = mean over items of 1[IoU >= k] (whether >= or > is not stated). Default temperature; mean of three runs. Overall: formula not stated, but Table 2 values match the item-weighted (pooled) mean over all 2,886 expressions (e.g. GPT-4.1 LLM: (76.19*189 + 17.28*1209 + 48.00*954 + 22.94*534)/2886 = 32.34). Results for other k thresholds are referenced to Appendix B.1 but not shown there. For 3D-VG models that output object IDs, the predicted box is that object's box from the scene graph.
Anywhere3D-Bench.Error type breakdown (Gemini-2.5-Pro): Each failure case is assigned to one of the three types by the definitions in Sec. 3.4, and the proportion of each type is reported (Fig. 7). Not stated: who assigns the labels, whether one error can have several types, and the exact counts.
Anywhere3D-Bench.Direction-to-axis mapping accuracy: 8 scenarios (4 facing axes x {left, right}), each run 3 times; accuracy = correct / 24 trials. How a response is judged correct is not stated. One reported value (Qwen2.5-72B right-handed 67.50%) is not a multiple of 1/24.
Anywhere3D-Bench.Accuracy gain from visual inputs / think: Delta = Acc@0.25IoU(MLLM setting) - Acc@0.25IoU(LLM setting) per level for the same model, averaged over GPT-4.1, o4-mini and Qwen2.5-VL-72B (object +8.19, part +4.76, space +3.47 points; e.g. object (5.88+7.13+11.55)/3 = 8.19). Thinking vs non-thinking margin = difference in Overall Acc@0.25IoU (e.g. Gemini-2.0-Flash, nearly 9 points).

Situat3DChange.GPT-based correctness score (GPT-score,: GPT-4o-mini (fixed timestamp 2024-07-18) rates each response s_i in 1..5 given the question, ground-truth answer and model response, using type-specific prompts: general QA (Fig. 18); egocentric direction on a clock face (Fig. 19: 5 if within 1 o'clock, 4 if the proximity direction is correct, 3 if adjacent, 2 if a significant error but not opposite, 1 if opposite); long-form text (Fig. 20: 5 fully correct ... 1 incorrect). C = (1/N) * sum_i (s_i - 1)/4 * 100%. Eq. 1 is introduced for QA; its use for the long-form 'GPT' column (following OpenEQA [71]) is implied but not stated explicitly.
Situat3DChange.Revised REL score (distance score): Per item: score = 1 if d_gt = 0 and d_pred = 0; 0 if d_gt = 0 and d_pred != 0; 1 - min(1, |d_pred - d_gt| / d_gt) if d_gt != 0 and d_pred != 0. This replaces REL = |d_pred - d_gt|/d_gt, which diverges when d_gt = 0. Not stated: the case d_gt != 0 and d_pred = 0, how the number is extracted from the response, and the aggregation (presumably mean over items x 100 to match the GPT-score range).
Situat3DChange.QA Average: Not stated. The Table 3 values equal the unweighted mean of the nine per-type scores (7 GPT-score types + 2 revised-REL types), e.g. DeepSeek-VL-7B 331.0/9 = 36.8.
Situat3DChange.CIDEr: Named only as a reference-based metric; formula and implementation not stated (standard TF-IDF-weighted n-gram CIDEr assumed).
Situat3DChange.BLEU-4: Named only; formula not stated (standard BLEU-4: geometric mean of 1-4-gram precisions times a brevity penalty assumed).
Situat3DChange.METEOR: Named only; formula not stated (standard METEOR assumed).
Situat3DChange.ROUGE: Named only; the ROUGE variant (e.g. ROUGE-L) and formula are not stated.
Situat3DChange.Sentence similarity (sim): Computed using a BERT-based model; the similarity function (e.g. cosine of sentence embeddings), the checkpoint and the aggregation are not stated.
Situat3DChange.EM@1 (and refined exact match): EM@1 = share of questions whose top-1 answer exactly matches a reference answer; values in parentheses follow the refined exact-match protocol from LEO [21]. Neither rule is spelled out in this paper.
Situat3DChange.Human evaluation score: Four human evaluators not involved in the project score the responses. The rating scale and how human scores are turned into the reported percentages are not stated (presumably the same 1-5 rubric rescaled as in Eq. 1).
Situat3DChange.Spearman correlation between GPT and hum: Spearman rank correlation between human scores and GPT-generated scores, following OpenEQA [71]; Average = mean of the three task correlations ((0.75+0.70+0.94)/3 = 0.80). Not stated: whether it is computed over per-sample scores or per-model aggregates, and how the four evaluators' scores are combined.
Situat3DChange.Run-to-run mean and standard deviation: Mean +/- standard deviation of each task score across runs with different random seeds. The text says four runs in total (the fixed-seed run plus three), while the table caption says 5 seeds; whether the std is sample or population std is not stated.

HouseLayout3D.F1 score @tau with entity distance d_E (: d_E(E,E') = max{ ||c_i - c'_pi(i)|| : i=1..4 }, the maximum distance between corresponding corners of two same-class rectangles, with corner permutation pi from Hungarian matching; a predicted entity counts as a match when d_E <= tau and precision / recall / F1 are then computed 'as in SceneScript [2]'. Entity-to-entity matching procedure and the tau values are not stated in the text (the results table is not in the md copy).
HouseLayout3D.F1 score @tau with generalized (Hausdorf: d_H(P,P') = max{ max_{v in V} D_pp(v,P'), max_{v' in V'} D_pp(v',P) }, the Hausdorff distance between polygon surfaces using the point-to-polygon distance D_pp (min distance from a point to any point on the polygon surface); d_H is used 'analogously to d_E' with threshold tau to compute F1. tau values and matching procedure not stated in the text.
HouseLayout3D.Depth accuracy Delta_tau: Delta_tau = (1/N) sum_{i=1..N} 1[ |D_pred(i) - D_GT(i)| <= tau ], with depth maps rendered at the input camera poses; on ScanNet++ object and window points are ignored via GT semantics. tau values not stated in the text (tables not in the md copy).
HouseLayout3D.Number of vertices (compactness): not stated (text only says methods differ in 'compactness (larger number of vertices)'; presumably the count of vertices in the predicted layout; the table itself is not in the md copy).

ReVSI.Accuracy (Acc, exact match): Acc = share of MCQ items whose predicted option exactly matches the ground-truth option (exact match), averaged over items of each task; GT answers are frame-budget specific (computed for the model's own inference frames).
ReVSI.Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA): MRA = (1/|C|) sum_{theta in C} 1( |y_hat - y| / y < 1 - theta ), C = {0.5, 0.55, ..., 0.95} (10 thresholds); averaged over items of each task.
ReVSI.Avg. (overall score): not stated in the text; the reported values equal the unweighted mean of the per-task scores (7 tasks at 64/32 frames, 5 at 16 frames), e.g. GPT-5.2 (56.2+41.5+73.9+63.0+48.4+34.9+38.2)/7 = 50.9.
ReVSI.Accuracy (Exact Match) on dummy videos (: Exact-match accuracy over 997 16-frame counting questions where the ground truth is always 0 (0 is the only correct answer): share of items with prediction == 0.
ReVSI.MRA on real vs. black dummy videos (obje: Same MRA formula as Eq. 1 (thresholds 0.5..0.95); which ground truth is used for the Black videos is not stated.
ReVSI.Relative Area Error (RAE): not stated (named 'Relative Area Error, measured against human annotations'; formula not given, presumably |A_VSI - A_human| / A_human).
ReVSI.Share of incorrect / ambiguous VSI-Bench: not stated beyond manual inspection of all associated QA pairs; shares shown in Figure 2 only (not in the md text).
ReVSI.Answerability and correctness under fram: Answerable = count (and %) of questions whose queried objects appear in the sampled frames; Correct = count (and %) whose answer computed from the sampled frames equals the all-frame GT (for tasks where the answer can change; else equals Answerable). Visibility rule stated for ReVSI construction: object visible if its pixel coverage in its most prominent frame exceeds 5% of the frame area, else manually annotated.
ReVSI.Absolute error (absolute distance task): not stated formally; |y_hat - y| in meters, shown per GT-distance bin (Figure 7).
ReVSI.Relative error (absolute distance task): not stated formally; implied |y_hat - y| / y as in the MRA formula, shown per GT-distance bin (Figure 7).

STRIDE-QA.Localization Success Rate (LSR): success s_t = 1[ |d_hat_t - d*_t| < 0.25 d*_t AND |theta_hat_t - theta*_t| < 10 deg ]; LSR@t = share of the 409 scene groups with s_t = 1. Angle wrap-around handling not stated.
STRIDE-QA.Mean Localization Success Rate (MLSR): MLSR = (1/G) sum_g (1/(T+1)) sum_{t=0..T} s_{g,t}, with s_{g,t} the LSR success bits and T = 3 (equals the mean of LSR@0..3s, e.g. (96.3+46.2+38.4+38.9)/4 = 55.0).
STRIDE-QA.Temporal Localization Consistency (TLC): TLC = (1/G) sum_g 1[ s_{g,0} AND s_{g,1} AND s_{g,2} AND s_{g,3} ], s_{g,t} = LSR success bits (distance within 25% and heading within 10 deg), T = 3.
STRIDE-QA.Per-dimension Success Rate (SR): SR = share of items whose prediction error is within tolerance: distance within +-25% of GT; heading within +-10 deg; velocity within +-20% of GT, switching to an absolute +-0.5 m/s tolerance when GT speed < 1.0 m/s.
STRIDE-QA.SpatialRGPT-Bench qualitative success ra: not stated (only 'success rates'); how a qualitative answer is judged correct is not given. Avg is not the plain mean of the category rates (e.g. GPT-4o original 80.47 vs 79.02), weighting not stated.
STRIDE-QA.SpatialRGPT-Bench quantitative success r: not stated in this paper (only 'success rates'); the paper cites the +-25% tolerance of Cheng et al. 2024 only when defining LSR; how the category rates combine into Quant. is not stated.
STRIDE-QA.mAP (detection, IoU@0.5:0.95): mean average precision averaged over IoU thresholds 0.5:0.95 and classes; range [0,1]; other details not stated ('standard metrics').
STRIDE-QA.mATE (mean Average Translation Error): not stated (standard nuScenes metric named only); range [0, inf) m.
STRIDE-QA.mASE (mean Average Scale Error): not stated (standard nuScenes metric named only); range [0,1].
STRIDE-QA.mAOE (mean Average Orientation Error): not stated (standard nuScenes metric named only); range [0, pi] rad.
STRIDE-QA.mAVE (mean Average Velocity Error): not stated (standard nuScenes metric named only); range [0, inf) m/s.
STRIDE-QA.AMOTA (Average Multi-Object Tracking Acc: not stated (standard metric named only); range [0,1].
STRIDE-QA.AMOTP (Average Multi-Object Tracking Pre: not stated (standard metric named only); range [0, inf) m.
STRIDE-QA.Recall (tracking): not stated (standard metric named only); range [0,1].
STRIDE-QA.IDSW (identity switches): not stated beyond a count of ID switches over the 100 validation scenes; range [0, inf).

VIR-Bench.Precision (macro-averaged): Correct prediction rules: prefecture / city node correct only on exact surface-name match with the gold label; POI correct if a 'lightweight sequence-matching' similarity > 0.7, or > 0.5 and the predicted POI category matches the gold category; edge correct only if the tuple <source, target, edge_type> exactly matches a gold tuple. Precision = correct predictions / predicted, macro-averaged (the averaging unit and matching algorithm are not stated; reported F1 differs from the harmonic mean of reported P and R, consistent with per-video averaging).
VIR-Bench.Recall (macro-averaged): Same correctness rules as precision (exact name match for prefecture/city; similarity > 0.7, or > 0.5 with matching category, for POIs; exact tuple match for edges); Recall = correct / gold, macro-averaged (averaging unit not stated).
VIR-Bench.F1 (macro-averaged): F1 from the same correctness rules, macro-averaged (averaging unit not stated; e.g. GPT-4.1 POI F1 53.6 vs 2PR/(P+R) = 55.6 from reported P, R).
VIR-Bench.Overall F1 (OVR): Weighted average of the per-type F1 scores (prefecture/city/POI for nodes; inclusion/transition for edges) with weights proportional to the number of elements in each type.
VIR-Bench.Attraction score (crowdsourced, 1-5): Each of 60 plans (20 videos x 3 settings) rated by 5 crowdworkers on a 5-point scale (5 = very appealing); score = mean rating (consistent with Table 10 distribution, e.g. POI 3.58); workers filtered by one check question.
VIR-Bench.Density score (crowdsourced, 1-5): 5 crowdworkers per plan choose 1-5; score = mean rating (3 is ideal, not higher-is-better); consistent with Table 10 (POI 2.96).
VIR-Bench.Alignment / Relevance score (crowdsource: 5 crowdworkers per plan choose 1 (completely unrelated) to 4 (follows the video); score = mean rating (consistent with Table 10: POI 0.10*4 + 0.25*3 + 0.54*2 + 0.11*1 = 2.34).
VIR-Bench.Transportation 'Has Info' (%): Crowdworkers choose among No info / Not navigable / Navigable; Has Info = 100% - share of 'No Info' ratings (e.g. POI 100 - 7 = 93.0).
VIR-Bench.Transportation 'Feasible' (%): not stated explicitly; the values equal Navigable / (Navigable + Not navigable) from Table 10 (e.g. POI 82/93 = 88.2%).
VIR-Bench.Selected vs. unselected POI difference (: POIs mentioned in a plan are extracted with GPT-4o and treated as selected; Delta = mean(selected) - mean(unselected) for on-screen duration (s) and Google rating (1-5); p < 0.05 / 0.01 / 0.001 marks, statistical test not stated.

SSI-Bench.Taskwise Accuracy: Acc_task = (1/N) sum_i 1[ pi_hat^(i) = pi*^(i) ] (exact match of the whole permutation). Output must parse as a Python list of length n whose entries are exactly {0..n-1}; otherwise the item scores 0. Random baseline 1/n! (12.85% overall). Whether the reported Avg is item-level or a mean over categories is not stated.
SSI-Bench.Pairwise Accuracy: Acc_pair(pi_hat, pi*) = (1/C(n,2)) sum_{0<=a<b<=n-1} 1[ (a before b in both) OR (b before a in both) ], averaged over the N instances; invalid outputs score 0; random baseline 1/2.
SSI-Bench.Thinking-token usage: Number of thinking tokens per question; for binning, expressed as a fraction of the maximum thinking-token count, then Taskwise Accuracy is computed per bucket. Bucket edges not stated.

SpatialAct.Accuracy (Basic Spatial Abilities): Accuracy = correct answers / questions, per task; the paper only says 'we use accuracy as the evaluation metric'. Questions are open-ended (counts, object ids, lists of ids) or multiple choice; the matching rule for open-ended answers (normalisation, list matching) is not stated.
SpatialAct.Accuracy (Single-step Error Detection an: Accuracy = correct answers / questions; multiple-choice detection and fix questions over scenes with injected layout errors. How detection and fix sub-questions are combined into one number is not stated.
SpatialAct.Repair Rate: Repair Rate = (E_before - E_after) / E_before, where E_before and E_after are the numbers of errors in the scenes before and after refinement (can be negative when the agent introduces new errors); max 30 turns, 8,096 completion tokens per turn. Whether it is computed per scene and averaged or pooled over all scenes is not stated; how the simulator detects and counts errors is not stated.
SpatialAct.Scene Success Rate: Scene Success Rate = (1/|S|) * sum over scenes s of I(E_after^s = 0), where E_after^s is the number of remaining errors in scene s after refinement.
SpatialAct.Effective Repair Turn Ratio: Effective Repair Turn Ratio = [sum over s in S of sum over t=1..T_s of I(E_t^s < E_(t-1)^s)] / [sum over s in S of T_s], where E_t^s is the errors remaining in scene s after turn t and T_s the number of turns for scene s (pooled over all turns).
SpatialAct.Premature Stop Rate (Pre. Stop): Premature Stop Rate = (1/|S|) * sum over s of I(E_(T_s)^s > 0), where E_(T_s)^s is the remaining errors at the end of interaction, either when the model decides to stop or when the maximum number of turns is reached.
SpatialAct.Average Completion Tokens per Scene (Tok: Avg. Completion Tokens = (1/|S|) * sum over s of C_s, where C_s is the total completion tokens generated by the model across all interaction turns for scene s.
SpatialAct.Self-selected Premature Stop Ratio (Self: Stated only in words: fraction of turns in which the model chooses to stop before reaching the maximum allowed iterations while errors remain (lower is better). Exact numerator/denominator formula not stated.
SpatialAct.Fix Rate (per error type): Not stated (reported only as 'Fix Rate' on the Figure 5c axis; presumably errors of a type fixed / errors of that type).
SpatialAct.Average iterations / operations per scen: Stated only as 'average iteration/operation per scene'; exact counting rule (e.g., whether a turn with several actions counts once) not stated.
SpatialAct.Pearson correlation between foundational: Pearson r between the per-model accuracy on a foundational task and the per-model Repair Rate (or Scene Success Rate); e.g., Single-step r = 0.817 with Repair Rate, 0.690 with Scene Success. Number of models used (presumably the 7 evaluated) not stated.

SceneActBench.ADD-S (Layout): d_surf(V^_i, V_j) = (1/|V^_i|) * sum over v^ in V^_i of min over v in V_j ||v^ - v||_2 (directed nearest-neighbour surface distance, metres). Hungarian assignment on C_ij = d_surf gives matched set M; ADD-S_scene = (1/|M|) * sum over (i,j) in M of d_surf(V^_i, V_j). At most 4,000 predicted vertices per mesh, each pair sampled to at most 2,000 points, seed 0. Extra predictions and unmatched targets do not enter the mean; a scene with no predicted object has no valid ADD-S and gets task score 0.
SceneActBench.Position Error (PE, Camera): PE = ||c^ - c||_2 using the final active camera's centre c^ and the ground-truth centre c.
SceneActBench.Angular Error (AE, Camera): AE = (180 deg / pi) * arccos(d^T d^) with unit view directions d^, d (the view direction is the negative local Z axis of the camera world matrix); range [0, 180] deg.
SceneActBench.Maximum Part Error (MPE, Articulated): MPE = max over movable parts i of {eps_i, (1 - kappa_i) * g_i}. g_i = max(mean_k ||V_op_ik - V_cl_ik||_2, 1e-6 m) (full travel); opening degree o_ti = Delta_ti / g_i; each predicted frame t is matched to the GT frame phi_i(t) in 0-16 with nearest opening degree; eps_i = max_t err_i(V^_ti, V_i^phi_i(t)) where err is mean corresponding-vertex L2 (or max of the two directed d_surf when topology differs); kappa_i = min(max_t o_ti, 1). Metres, no size normalisation; an unmoved part is charged its full travel.
SceneActBench.F@5% (object-level, Reconstruction): Fixed-scale ICP (scale = ratio of bbox diagonals; yaw inits 0/90/180/270; <=30 iterations) aligns the merged prediction; DBSCAN (radii 0.10-0.40 x mean GT diagonal, >=0.04 m, min_samples 10, clusters <30 points removed; K closest to N, 0.5 penalty if K < N) splits it; Hungarian matching on cluster means, matches farther than 0.6*delta_scene rejected; matched clusters recentred. tau_j = 0.05 * delta_j (GT bbox diagonal). Prec_j = share of predicted points within tau_j of GT, Rec_j = share of GT points within tau_j of prediction; unmatched objects get 0. F@5% = (1/N) * sum over j of 2*Prec_j*Rec_j/(Prec_j + Rec_j) (0 when the denominator is 0). Scene with <10 points is invalid.
SceneActBench.Maximum Mover Error (MME, Dynamic): Hungarian matching of mover-centroid tracks (cost = mean per-frame distance), one global translation (xy mean, z median of pooled paired differences) applied, rematching. e_i = (1/(m_i * S)) * sum over r=1..m_i of ||p^_r,sigma(i) - p_r,i||_2 with m_i the shorter track length and S = max(max xy extent of GT locations, 5 m) (40 m if empty); unmatched GT movers get e_i = 1; MME = max over GT movers of e_i. Extra predicted movers ignored; no predicted mover -> MME = 1. Rotation and scale not corrected.
SceneActBench.Layout Error (LE, Dynamic): d_stat(X^_stat, X_stat) = mean over x^ of min over x ||x^ - x||_2 + mean over x of min over x^ ||x - x^||_2 (after the same global translation); LE = d_stat / (2S). LE = 1 if no predicted static objects; scene invalid if GT static set is empty.
SceneActBench.Task score: q_down(m; u) = 100 * max(0, 1 - m/u) for errors, q_up(m; u) = 100 * min(1, m/u) for F@5%. Layout q_down(ADD-S; 4 m); Camera = mean of q_down(PE; 4 m) and q_down(AE; 90 deg) per case; Articulated q_down(MPE; 1); Reconstruction q_up(F@5%; 1); Dynamic = mean of q_down(MME; 1) and q_down(LE; 1) per case. Missing, invalid or non-finite values score 0. Task score = mean of case scores.
SceneActBench.Overall score: Overall = mean of the five task scores (each the mean of 0-100 case scores); multi-view Layout and photo-realistic Dynamic are excluded.
SceneActBench.Position error (Layout audit, PosErr_lay: PosErr_layout = (1/|M|) * sum over matched (i,j) of ||b(V^_i) - b(V_j)||_2, where b is the bounding-box centre; metres. Audit metric, not in Overall.
SceneActBench.Chamfer (Layout scene-level symmetric su: d<->_surf(V^_scene, V_scene) = d_surf(V^_scene, V_scene) + d_surf(V_scene, V^_scene) on merged surfaces sampled to at most 20,000 points each; metres, unnormalised, no object matching.
SceneActBench.Placement accuracy (PA, Layout): PA = (1/N) * sum over GT objects j of 1[xi_j < 0.1 * delta_j], where xi_j = matched ADD-S cost C_i(j)j (+inf if unmatched) and delta_j = GT bbox diagonal.
SceneActBench.Binary scene success (SS, Layout): SS = 1 only when the predicted object count is correct and PA = 1, else 0; reported scene-success rate = mean of SS over scenes.
SceneActBench.Predicted FOV (Camera audit): Recorded from the final active camera; the evaluator does not compute |f^_x - f_x|, so it is an audit value, not an error metric, and does not affect PE, AE or scores.
SceneActBench.SSIM (render audit): Final scene rendered at 384x384 (EEVEE, same world settings; Camera uses predicted FOV for both renders), resized to 256x256, RGB in [0,1], data range 1; SSIM between the two renders. How the four Reconstruction orbit views are combined is not stated. Audit only.
SceneActBench.PSNR (render audit): Same render pair as SSIM (384x384 renders resized to 256x256, RGB in [0,1], data range 1); PSNR between them. Orbit-view aggregation not stated. Audit only.
SceneActBench.OpenCLIP similarity / distance (render a: Cosine similarity s_CLIP between OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 image embeddings of the two renders; distance reported as 1 - s_CLIP. Orbit-view aggregation not stated. Audit only.
SceneActBench.LPIPS (render audit): AlexNet LPIPS on the 256x256 render pair. Orbit-view aggregation not stated. Audit only.
SceneActBench.Mean Part Error (Articulated): Mean Part Error averages the aligned per-part errors instead of taking their maximum (whether the (1 - kappa_i) * g_i motion term is included is not stated).
SceneActBench.Open-state ADD-S (Articulated): Compares the complete agent open keyframe with ground-truth frame 16 using ADD-S; the exact matching/averaging details for this global variant are not stated.
SceneActBench.Movable recall (MR, Articulated): Part i is recovered when g_i > 1e-3 m and a_i > 0.2 * g_i, with a_i the displacement of its predicted part centre between the selected closed and open keyframes; MR = recovered movable parts / movable parts (0 for empty sets). Pooled counts (moved / GT parts) are shown in Figure 10.
SceneActBench.False-move rate (FMR, Articulated): h_s = mean of the largest 1% closed-to-open vertex displacements of static part s (max if fewer than 100 vertices; bidirectional NN displacements if topology differs); FMR = share of static parts with h_s > 0.05 m (0 for empty sets).
SceneActBench.Type-mismatch rate (Articulated): Eligible parts: mean predicted vertex displacement > max(0.05 m, 0.25 * g_i). Rotation inferred when fitted rotation > 15 deg; else translation when fitted translation > 0.1 x target range (translational joint) or 0.05 m (rotational joint). Rate = eligible parts with inferred type != target type / eligible parts; 0 when none eligible.
SceneActBench.Reverse-direction rate (Articulated): Direction fitted from predicted and GT endpoint geometry; a part is reversed when their directional cosine < -0.7 (cosines between -0.7 and 0.7 counted as off-axis, not reversed); rate = reversed eligible parts / eligible parts (same eligibility as type-mismatch; 0 when none).
SceneActBench.Merged-scene F@tau (F@2%, F@5%, F@10%, R: After fixed-scale ICP on 4,000-point merged sets: F_scene(tau) = 2 * Prec_scene(tau) * Rec_scene(tau) / (Prec_scene(tau) + Rec_scene(tau)) (0 if denominator 0), tau in {0.02, 0.05, 0.10} x delta_scene (GT scene bbox diagonal). Audit only.
SceneActBench.Chamfer (aligned, Reconstruction): d<->_surf(V^_scene, V_scene) = d_surf(A,B) + d_surf(B,A) on the same 4,000-point ICP-aligned sets. Audit only.
SceneActBench.Region object F@5% (Reconstruction): Each GT box expanded by 0.1 * delta_scene; aligned predicted points inside are scored with local F@5% (0 if fewer than 10 predicted points); averaged over GT objects without cluster matching or recentring. Audit only.
SceneActBench.Object coverage (Reconstruction): Fraction of GT objects whose region F@5% >= 0.30. Pooled counts (covered / targets) also in Figure 10 and Table 6.
SceneActBench.Match rate (Reconstruction): Match rate = accepted Hungarian matches / N (matches farther than 0.6 * delta_scene rejected). Pooled counts (matched / targets) also in Figure 10.
SceneActBench.Mean centroid error (Reconstruction): Mean of pre-translation cluster-to-ground-truth mean distances over accepted matches.
SceneActBench.Point-BERT similarity (object and scene,: Cosine similarity between OpenShape openshape-pointbert-vitb32-rgb embeddings; each set sampled or repeated to 10,000 points, centred, scaled to unit max radius, neutral-grey RGB. Scene uses the globally aligned surfaces; object uses the GT box expanded by 0.1 * delta_scene (fewer than 100 predicted points -> 0), averaged over all GT objects. Audit only.
SceneActBench.Average Mover Error (AME, Dynamic): AME = (1/N_mov) * sum over GT movers of e_i, including the 1.0 penalties for unmatched movers; AME = 1 if no predicted mover.
SceneActBench.Movable recall (Dynamic): Movable recall = |M_trk| / N_mov; 0 if no predicted mover exists. Pooled counts (matched / GT movers) also in Figure 10.
SceneActBench.Path-shape error (Dynamic): q(P) = [||P_T - P_1||/S, L(P)/S, ||P_T - P_1||/(L(P) + 1e-9), (max P_z - min P_z)/S, l_perp(P)/S], with segments longer than 0.3S treated as teleports and excluded from path length L(P). e_shape = (1/(5*|M_trk|)) * sum over matched (k,i) of ||q(P^_k) - q(P_i)||_1 (the md renders the factor as '15|M trk|'); 1 when no mover is matched.
SceneActBench.Direction-error rate (Dynamic): Direction = first principal axis of each centred track, sign by net displacement; rate = share of matched, moving (L(P) > 0.05 S), non-closed (net displacement >= 0.1 L(P)) GT tracks whose predicted and GT axes differ by >= 30 deg. Pooled counts in Figure 10 / Table 6.
SceneActBench.Heading error (Dynamic): theta_r = atan2(dy_r, dx_r); XY steps below 0.005 S and above 8x the median retained step removed; total turning = sum of absolute wrapped heading changes; per mover |turning_pred - turning_GT| / (2*pi) capped at 1; averaged over matched movers with moving GT tracks (closed loops included); 0 when none is moving.
SceneActBench.Scale error (Dynamic): Isotropic XY scale estimated by least squares on centred pooled points in the coarse alignment, bounded to [0.1, 10] and not applied; scale error = |log(scale)|; 0 when there is too little variation to estimate scale.
SceneActBench.Size error (static scene, Dynamic): Ground slabs removed (XY span > 5x median span and height < 1/8 of that span); axes shorter than 0.1 m omitted; size error = mean over valid axes of |log(s^_a / s_a)|. Outside Dynamic scoring.
SceneActBench.Mover-size error (Dynamic): Per matched mover: mean over valid axes (axes shorter than 0.05 m omitted; skinned movers use Blender-evaluated boxes) of |log(s^_a / s_a)|; then mean over movers. Outside Dynamic scoring.
SceneActBench.Denominator-aware failure-stage rates: Rate = pooled successes / pooled denominator with exact counts; rows marked dagger use conditional denominators (parts with measurable rigid motion; eligible matched non-loop movers). Camera 'avoids joint cap' counts cases that avoid simultaneous PE >= 4 m and AE >= 90 deg. 0/0 means no eligible evidence.
SceneActBench.Task-correlation matrix (Pearson): Z in R^(11x5) holds each configuration's five fixed-reference task scores (Camera PE/AE average, Dynamic MME/LE average); standard Pearson correlation between each pair of columns; symmetric, ones on the diagonal.
SceneActBench.Spearman correlation between case-level: Spearman rank correlation of case-level PE and AE (reported 0.76-0.93 for the top three configurations); nothing else stated.
SceneActBench.Bootstrap rank-first frequency: 50,000 paired case resamples; share of resamples in which each configuration has the highest Overall, plus 95% intervals for Overall gaps. Measures sensitivity to benchmark composition, not run-to-run variation.
SceneActBench.Task-score change between paired conditi: Delta = task score(alternate) - task score(base), in points, over paired cases (100 Layout, 10 Dynamic scenes); CLI comparison Delta = CLI minus harness.
SceneActBench.Task contribution to Overall gap: Contribution = (task-score difference) / 5; the five contributions sum exactly to the Overall gap (linear decomposition).
SceneActBench.Task-balanced realised budget fraction a: Realised steps (capped at MaxSteps, from the scored trace prefix) / MaxSteps, averaged within each task, then equally across the five tasks; tool calls counted from the same prefix and task-balanced the same way; Spearman rho between budget fraction and Overall across 11 configurations.
SceneActBench.Step-budget sensitivity (checkpoint re-s: Selected execution checkpoints are retrospectively scored with the same per-case scoring rule under a common MaxSteps value for all tasks at each curve point; reports Overall and task scores per budget. Checkpoint selection rule not stated.

ESI-Bench.Accuracy: A response is correct if y^ = y* (final answer committed with answer(y^, c) within T_max = 30 steps); accuracy (%) on matched subsets. Answers are free-form, with format implied by the question (yes/no, category, integer, ordering); the normalisation or matching of free-form answers is not stated. How subcategories are averaged into category rows is not stated.
ESI-Bench.Average active exploration steps to a co: Stated only as 'average number of active exploration steps to reach a correct answer'; presumably mean step count over correctly answered active trajectories; exact rule not stated.
ESI-Bench.View Diversity: Percentage of trajectories containing observations from multiple meaningfully distinct viewpoints; how 'meaningfully distinct' is decided (annotator or rule) is not stated.
ESI-Bench.Contrastive View Rate: Percentage of trajectories containing at least one contrastive observation; the paper says this can be estimated by annotating each new view as redundant, confirmatory or contrastive, but who annotates and how is not stated.
ESI-Bench.Belief Revision Rate: Percentage of trajectories where the predicted answer changes after additional observations; how intermediate answers are elicited or extracted is not stated.
ESI-Bench.Number of emergent strategy clusters: Human annotators group successful active trajectories by high-level behavioural pattern without predefined labels; metric = number of distinct clusters per subcategory.
ESI-Bench.Absolute Gap (GPT-4o-generated vs human-: Absolute Gap = accuracy(GPT-4o-generated subset) - accuracy(human-generated subset), subsets matched on category distribution.

SpatialWorld.Task Success Rate (TSR): TSR = (1/N) * sum over tasks i of 1[V_i(s_T^(i)) = 1], where V_i is a task-specific human-annotated verifier script querying the terminal state s_T^(i); episode ends at EndTask or step budget 2g + 10 (g = human golden action count); temperature 1.0, 30-turn window. Physical Overall is a weighted average of the Daily, Work, Entertain., Travel and Social categories (weights not stated). Snake3D uses a scale-normalised score instead of binary success.
SpatialWorld.Step Efficiency (SE): SE = (1/|S|) * sum over successful tasks i in S of n_i* / n_i, where n_i is the agent's step count and n_i* the human-annotated reference length. Physical Overall is the weighted mean over successful valid physical trajectories ('--' when no success).
SpatialWorld.Scale-normalised discrete score (Snake3D: Score = achieved snake score / spatial edge length of the game environment; used instead of the binary success indicator for Snake3D. Clipping and how it enters TSR averages are not stated.
SpatialWorld.Delta TSR (continuous minus discrete act: Delta TSR = TSR_continuous - TSR_discrete in percentage points; positive favours continuous action parameters.
SpatialWorld.Failure-type composition: Share of failed tasks by terminal failure type from failure logs (e.g., 32.4% premature DONE, 48.5% explicit FAIL for GPT-5.4); classification rule from logs not stated.
SpatialWorld.Median step count on successful / failed: Median number of steps over successful tasks and over failed tasks, per model.

VisGym.Task success rate (average task success: On the stop action the environment computes a binary reward from the final environment state (reward 0 for non-terminal transitions); success thresholds come from task difficulty parameters (e.g., Colorization accuracy radius 11/16, Matchstick Rotation position tolerance 10/5 and angular tolerance 15/10, Mental Rotation 2D angular tolerance 10/5 deg, Mental Rotation 3D Objaverse 15/5 deg). Step limit 20 (easy, Dot-Pointing, Fetch-Reach) or 30 (hard, Fetch Pick-and-Place); 70 episodes per task and setting; average = mean over tasks. Per-task success conditions beyond these tolerances, and scoring of episodes truncated without stop, are not stated. Error bars are standard error of the mean.
VisGym.Steps taken on successful trajectories: Count steps per trajectory; density curve and per-model mean over successful trajectories (Figure 3); histogram over all trajectories split by correct/incorrect (Figure 18).
VisGym.Failure-pattern frequency: StringSight clusters behaviours extracted by a GPT-4.1 annotator; then GPT-4.1 labels every trace for the four behaviours (multi-label); frequency = traces with the behaviour / traces.
VisGym.Final angular error (Mental Rotation 3D: Reported as 'final angular error on the test set'; formula (which angle distance, how averaged) not stated.
VisGym.Easy-to-Hard performance drop: Per task: mean accuracy over all models on Easy minus mean accuracy on Hard.
VisGym.Per-task model ranking: Rank models by task success rate; ties receive the worse (higher) rank (two models tied for best both get rank 2).
VisGym.Vision Gain / LLM Gain: Vision Gain = success(fine-tune both) - success(fine-tune LLM only); LLM Gain = success(fine-tune both) - success(fine-tune vision only).
VisGym.Identical-image misjudgment rate: On 100 pairs of initial and final-goal observations, prompt 'Do the two images look exactly the same?'; rate = pairs wrongly judged identical / 100.

MineAnyBuild.Evaluation Score (GPT-4.1 critic): GPT-4.1 grades each sub-dimension 1-10 from Replay Mod frames of the executed blueprint. Creativity: S_Eval = 0.8*Creativity + 0.05*(Completeness + Complexity + Architecture Structure + Overall Aesthetic/Atmosphere/Fidelity). Executable Spatial Plan Generation: S_Eval = 0.4*Completeness(Instruction Following) + 0.3*Complexity + 0.3*OAAF, with a human reference image scored 8 by default as anchor. Spatial Understanding: S_Eval = Completeness(Instruction Following), reference scored 10. Non-executable plans get 0. Averaging over items not stated.
MineAnyBuild.Matching Score (block match): S_Matching = (M / N) * 10, N = ground-truth block count, M = matching blocks in the 3D bounding space excluding 'air'; a block counts only if its type matches at the same relative position. Weighted 0.05 (0.05-0.1) in task scores.
MineAnyBuild.Voting Score (Swiss-round critic battles: Multi-round battle: each round agents sorted by (-score, id) and paired with not-yet-compared opponents; GPT-4.1 picks the better of each pair (winner +1, loser -1); after R rounds S_Voting = 3 + 5 * (score - min(score)) / (max(score) - min(score)). Weight ~0.05; 'whether to use this score' depends on evaluation scale. Number of rounds R not stated.
MineAnyBuild.Executable Spatial Plan Generation Score: S_SP = k3 * S_Evaluation + k4 * S_Matching with k4 = 0.05, k3 = 0.95; the paper also says that for most cases only the Evaluation Score is used. Non-executable outputs score 0.
